system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING
PHYSICS CHECK — governing physical relation: Fick's law of diffusion for water vapor through polymers. Water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) depends on permeability coefficient, thickness, and vapor pressure gradient. The plasticization effect increases the permeability coefficient exponentially with moisture content. USER CONSTRAINT: WVTR must remain below 0.5 g/m2/day over 18 months at 25°C and 65% RH.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — components: (1) Add 5-10 nm aluminum oxide (Al2O3) atomic layer deposition (ALD) coating on the ethylene-vinyl alcohol (EVOH) layer, (2) Maintain standard polymer film structure (polyethylene/EVOH/polyethylene), (3) Use commercial ALD coating equipment with precursors trimethylaluminum and water vapor. Materials: EVOH copolymer (32 mol% ethylene), polyethylene layers, Al2O3 ALD coating. Procedure: Apply ALD coating to EVOH layer after extrusion and before lamination to other polymer layers.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — implementation burden: comparable to standard practice for high-barrier packaging (similar equipment costs and process steps), but adds a vacuum coating step. Operability: slightly more complex due to ALD process control requirements. Maintenance: standard for vacuum coating equipment. Cost class: medium-high (20-30% increase over standard high-barrier film), justified by extended shelf life and reduced food waste.
EXECUTABLE TEST — falsification test: protocol: (1) Prepare test samples with and without ALD coating (n=10 per group), (2) Condition samples at 25°C and 65% RH for 18 months, (3) Measure WVTR using ASTM F1249 standard method at 0, 3, 6, 12, and 18 months, (4) Measure oxygen transmission rate (OTR) at same intervals. Instruments: MOCON PERMATRAN-W® WVTR tester, MOCON OX-TRAN® OTR tester, environmental chamber. Pass/fail threshold: WVTR must remain ≤0.5 g/m2/day and OTR must remain ≤10 cc/m2/day at all measurement points. Duration: 18 months with measurements at specified intervals.
